doc.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998

title: V-discs and the Army in the Philippines
summary: Army Special Services sent V-discs overseas and Avakian smuggled some home.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Oh definitely. The Army Special Services, which was the branch that took care of morale and so forth, managed to get even V-discs over to the Phillipines and I copped a few for myself which I wasn’t supposed to do, and hid them in my barracks bag and brought some back home actually. And V-discs were quite remarkable. They were twelve-inch flexible vinylite records, had to be in order to survive transportation and so forth, and the Army or Navy, Marine Corps, all received copies of these recordings and they were used mainly in the centers where there were recreational facilities for the soldiers, and that’s how I swiped a few. They were either copied from released records, but more and more they were made especially for our armed forces, in studios and performances and so on. Collectors are really quite into this whole thing and there are some wonderful performances, but that’s a different matter, we won’t go into it.
